name: Kingdom of Navarre
alt: Kingdom of Pamplona (restored 1134, styled 'of Navarre' from Sancho VI)

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Aragon
predecessors.text: the Navarrese part of the union of Aragon and Navarre; the cortes of Aragon and Navarre 'chose separate kings' in 1134

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Pamplona
predecessors.text: the same kingdom restored: 'originally the Kingdom of Pamplona'

successors.name: Crown of Castile
successors.text: Iberian Navarre, 'Upper Navarre', annexed to Castile in 1515 after the invasion of 1512

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: Lower Navarre, incorporated into France between 1620 and 1624

ledger.x: 1134: after Alfonso the Battler's death Navarre and Aragon 'chose separate kings' and García Ramírez, 'the Restorer', is the first to use the title King of Navarre.
1135: García Ramírez holds Zaragoza as a fief.
1136: García is forced to give up La Rioja.
1137: Zaragoza is surrendered.
1146: García occupies Tauste.
1146: Alfonso VII mediates peace between Navarre and Aragon over Tauste ('Alfonso VII mediated a peace between the two kingdoms').
1157: Sancho VI recovers Artajona.
1173: Castilian invasions begin.
1177: Henry II of England's arbitration settles the Castilian dispute.
1199: Alfonso VIII invades western Navarre.
1200: Castile completes the conquest of western Navarre.
1200: the fighting for western Navarre ends with the conquest complete; the 1207 truce at Guadalajara only confirms it.
1234 (7 April): Sancho VII dies at Tudela and the crown passes to his nephew Theobald of Champagne.
1284: Joan I of Navarre marries the future Philip IV of France and Navarre passes under the French crown.
1328: Charles I (Charles IV of France) dies and Joanna II succeeds, ending the union with France.
1463 (23 April): Castile's hold on the Sonsierra and Los Arcos is upheld at Bayonne.

1479: John II dies and 'Queen Eleanor succeeded him for only 15 days and then died', leaving the crown to Francis Phoebus; Eleanor was Countess of Foix and Béarn, so the crown passes to the Foix line (Navarre page).
1512 (19 July): Ferdinand of Aragon invades Navarre.
1512: Upper Navarre falls to the Spanish.
1512: the Albret court leaves Pamplona.
1512: the Spanish hold Iberian Navarre; John III's October counter-attack on Pamplona fails (Navarre page: 'attacked Pamplona without success' in October 1512).
1521 (May): Pamplona revolts and the Franco-Navarrese reconquer Navarre.

1521 (30 June): the Franco-Navarrese are 'completely defeated at the Battle of Esquiroz' (Noáin) and Upper Navarre is lost again; the page says Southern Navarre was 'permanently annexed in 1524' on the Navarre page.
1521 (September): the second campaign opens at the Bidasoa.
1524 (19 February): Hondarribia surrenders.
1525: Spain takes Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port.
1527: local lords retake Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port ('Local lords retook it in 1527'); 'Spain abandoned the region in 1528, except for an outpost at Luzaide/Valcarlos'.
1589: Henry III of Navarre becomes Henry IV of France.
1620: Lower Navarre passes to France.
1620: the Kingdom of Navarre ends as a separate kingdom, merged into France ('Between 1620 and 1624'); the Parliament of Navarre sits at Pau, and the French kings keep the title.

wars.name: García Ramírez's war with Alfonso VII
wars.outcome: '1137: García allied with Alfonso I of Portugal and confronted Alfonso VII'; '1139-1140: a peace between the two was confirmed'.

wars.name: Navarrese-Aragonese incident at Tauste
wars.outcome: García occupied Tauste, which belonged to Aragon; Alfonso VII mediated a peace between the two kingdoms.

wars.name: Castilian invasions of Navarre under Alfonso VIII
wars.outcome: Henry II of England's arbitration of 1177 'decided to refer them back to the boundaries' of 1158, 'which confirmed the loss of Bureba and Rioja'.

wars.name: Castilian conquest of western Navarre
wars.outcome: Álava, Guipúzcoa and Biscay lost to Castile by 1200; the Treaty of Guadalajara (1207) sealed a 5-year truce over the occupied territories and confirmed the conquests.

wars.name: Navarrese civil war of the Agramonts and Beaumonts
wars.outcome: 'In 1451 Navarre split in two confederacies, the Agramonts and the Beaumonts'; Prince Charles was 'defeated by his father at Aibar in 1451' and died in 1461.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of Iberian Navarre
wars.outcome: Castilian-Aragonese victory: Iberian Navarre annexed to Castile (Cortes of Burgos, June 1515); reconquests of 1516 and 1521-1524 failed; the Treaty of Cambrai (1529) 'sealed the division of Navarre along the Pyrenees', leaving Lower Navarre independent under…

certainty.note: Lower Navarre is a small kingdom whose Pyrenean edge with Spain was 'sealed' by the Treaty of Cambrai (1529); the Navarre page says the Treaty of the Pyrenees of 1659 'put an end to the litigation over the definite French-Spanish borders'…
